subject: pharmacology
title: CNS Stimulants, ADHD and Dependence: Amphetamine, Methylphenidate, Modafinil, Cocaine and Nicotine Therapies

steps.tx: **Amphetamine** reverses monoamine transporters, flooding synapses with dopamine, noradrenaline (and serotonin at high dose): wakefulness, euphoria, appetite suppression, sympathomimetic cardiovascular stimulation, and with excess, hyperthermia, psychosis indistinguishable from paranoid schizophrenia, and seizures. Mixed amphetamine salts and lisdexamfetamine (a prodrug smoothing onset and deterring injection misuse) treat ADHD and narcolepsy; illicit methamphetamine's neurotoxicity and dependence write the public health counterpoint.
steps.say: Amphetamine empties the monoamine terminals; therapy and toxicity are the same flood at different depths.

steps.tx: **Amphetamine** reverses transporters for monoamines, so dopamine and noradrenaline flood the synapse, and serotonin joins them at high dose. Clinically that flood is wakefulness, euphoria, loss of appetite and a sympathomimetic rise in pulse and pressure. Excess produces hyperthermia, seizures, and a psychosis that the mental state alone cannot separate from paranoid schizophrenia. Mixed salts, and lisdexamfetamine as a prodrug with a smoother onset that is harder to inject, are the forms used for ADHD and narcolepsy. Illicit methamphetamine adds neurotoxicity and a heavy dependence burden.
steps.say: Amphetamine reverses monoamine transporters and empties dopamine and noradrenaline into the synapse. The same flood causes alertness, euphoria and a fast pulse at treatment doses, and hyperthermia, seizures and a paranoid psychosis when the dose is too high. Salt mixtures and the prodrug lisdexamfetamine treat ADHD and narcolepsy. Illicit methamphetamine is neurotoxic and strongly dependence producing.

vis.alt: A synapse shows amphetamine reversing the dopamine transporter so that vesicle contents empty into the cleft.
vis.caption: Amphetamine runs the dopamine transporter backwards and empties vesicular dopamine into the synaptic cleft. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Methylphenidate** blocks dopamine and noradrenaline transporters without reversing them, a gentler mechanistic cousin that is first line for ADHD in most guidelines alongside amphetamines, in immediate and osmotic extended release forms engineered for school day coverage. Appetite suppression and growth velocity, insomnia, tics unmasked (not caused, modern data argue), and cardiovascular screening by history form its review list; diversion to peers is counselled as frankly as any adverse effect.
steps.say: Methylphenidate blocks the pump instead of reversing it; growth, sleep and diversion are its review list.

left.title: Methylphenidate profile
points: DAT and NET blockade, no transporter reversal
Immediate and extended release (OROS) formulations
First line ADHD pharmacotherapy with amphetamines
Response assessed by teachers and parents, not only clinic

right.title: Review list
points: Appetite, weight and growth velocity charted
Sleep onset delayed: dose timing adjusted
Pulse and pressure at titration and annually
Diversion and misuse counselled in adolescents

steps.tx: After a cardiac history, most guidelines start attention-deficit treatment with methylphenidate or an amphetamine. Tics, marked anxiety, or a home where tablets may be diverted, move the choice off that rung. **Atomoxetine** blocks noradrenaline reuptake, does not occupy the dopamine transporter as a stimulant does, and takes weeks to work. Guanfacine is the option when sleep and tics dominate and a stimulant has failed. The comorbidity chooses the rung.
steps.say: Stimulants are the usual first treatment for ADHD. Atomoxetine is the non-stimulant when tics, anxiety or diversion risk make a stimulant a poor start. Guanfacine is considered when sleep and tics lead the picture.

vis.alt: ADHD treatment ladder placing a stimulant, atomoxetine and guanfacine according to comorbidity.
vis.caption: A stimulant is the first rung, with atomoxetine and guanfacine as the alternatives when tics, anxiety or a risk of diversion change the choice. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **ADHD** pharmacotherapy stratifies by age and comorbidity: stimulants carry the largest effect sizes (around 1.0) in school age children, atomoxetine and alpha 2 agonists (guanfacine, clonidine) serve where tics, anxiety, misuse risk or stimulant intolerance argue, and preschoolers start with behavioural therapy. Medication holidays, growth charts and academic versus weekend coverage are negotiated per child, because the disorder is developmental and the prescription is only one scaffold among educational and family ones.
steps.say: Stimulants lead for effect size; atomoxetine and guanfacine cover the comorbidity corners, behaviour first in the youngest.

nodes.label: ADHD confirmed across settings with impairment
Behavioural and educational scaffolds in place
Stimulant titrated to teacher and parent report
Growth, sleep, pulse and diversion reviewed serially

steps.tx: **Modafinil** promotes wakefulness by a mechanism still argued (weak dopamine transporter inhibition with hypothalamic downstream effects) in narcolepsy, shift work disorder and obstructive apnoea residual sleepiness, with less euphoria and abuse scheduling than amphetamines and rare severe skin reactions (Stevens Johnson) in its warnings. It induces CYP3A4 enough to compromise hormonal contraception, a counselling point with real pregnancies behind it. Armodafinil is its longer lived enantiomer.
steps.say: Modafinil wakes without much euphoria, induces contraceptive failure quietly, and rarely rashes dangerously.

left.title: Modafinil territory
points: Narcolepsy and shift work sleep disorder
Residual apnoea sleepiness adjunct
Lower abuse scheduling than amphetamines
Headache and nausea commonest

right.title: Modafinil cautions
points: CYP3A4 induction: contraceptive failure risk
Rare Stevens Johnson syndrome: stop for rash
Psychiatric symptoms in predisposed patients
Not a substitute for treating apnoea itself

steps.tx: **Atomoxetine**, a selective noradrenaline reuptake inhibitor, treats ADHD without stimulant scheduling or tic anxiety, needing two to six weeks for effect, carrying hepatic warnings, a small suicidality signal in youth labelling, and noradrenergic tolls (appetite, pulse, pressure, urinary hesitancy). It suits families refusing stimulants, comorbid tic or anxiety presentations, and households where diversion is a live risk, trading onset speed for calm logistics.
steps.say: Atomoxetine is the slow, unscheduled ADHD option for tic, anxiety and diversion haunted households.

left.title: Atomoxetine advantages
points: No controlled scheduling or misuse market
Tic and anxiety comorbidity friendly
Once daily, evening or morning flexibility
No growth effect of stimulant magnitude debated less

right.title: Atomoxetine burdens
points: Two to six weeks to judge effect
Nausea, appetite loss, somnolence or insomnia
Rare hepatic injury: jaundice warnings
Pulse and pressure monitored as with stimulants

steps.tx: **Caffeine**, adenosine receptor antagonism in a beverage, is the world's stimulant and a legitimate drug in neonatal apnoea of prematurity (caffeine citrate), analgesic adjuvancy and post dural puncture headache tradition. **Doxapram**, a carotid body and medullary stimulant, survives as a respiratory stimulant of historical and niche interest. Both illustrate that stimulant is a dose and context word: caffeine's withdrawal headache closes the dependence loop that the whole lesson keeps meeting.
steps.say: Caffeine is the licensed stimulant everyone self prescribes; doxapram is its museum grade respiratory cousin.

nodes.label: Caffeine blocks adenosine A1 and A2A receptors
Neonatal apnoea: caffeine citrate stimulates drive

steps.tx: The illicit stimulant and hallucinogen shelf maps by syndrome for examinations: **cocaine** (transporter blockade, vasospasm, hyperthermia; benzodiazepines cool its agitation, beta blockers avoided unopposed), cannabis (CB1 agonism, adolescent psychosis risk), LSD (5 HT2A agonism, hallucinogen persisting perception rarely), phencyclidine (NMDA antagonism, violent agitation, nystagmus), and MDMA (serotonin flood: hyperthermia, hyponatraemia, serotonin syndrome). Management across the shelf is cooling, benzodiazepines and time, tailored by toxidrome.
steps.say: Cool, sedate with benzodiazepines, and read the toxidrome; beta blockers stay holstered in cocaine toxicity.

left.title: Stimulant toxidromes
points: Cocaine: vasospasm infarctions, hyperthermia, seizures
MDMA: serotonin excess, hyponatraemia, hyperthermia
Amphetamines: psychosis, hyperthermia, rhabdomyolysis
Shared care: benzodiazepines, cooling, fluids

right.title: Dissociative and hallucinogen notes
points: Phencyclidine: NMDA blockade, agitation, nystagmus
LSD: 5 HT2A hallucinosis, supportive calm environment
Cannabis: CB1 effects, adolescent psychosis association
Withdrawal syndromes milder than depressant classes

steps.tx: Nicotine dependence pharmacotherapy closes the dependence arc: **nicotine replacement** in patch plus short acting combinations doubles quit rates, **varenicline** (alpha 4 beta 2 partial agonist) roughly doubles to triples them as the most effective single agent, and bupropion assists where depression argues. **Drug dependence** treatment principles generalise from here and the opioid lessons: substitution or partial agonism, contingency management, relapse as a treatment signal rather than moral failure, and withdrawal syndromes graded by class danger (alcohol and benzodiazepine withdrawals kill; stimulant and opioid withdrawals torment).
steps.say: Varenicline leads quitting, combinations follow, and withdrawal danger, not discomfort, ranks depressants above stimulants.

left.title: Smoking cessation league
points: Varenicline: most effective monotherapy
Combination NRT (patch plus gum or lozenge) next
Bupropion where mood argues
Behavioural support multiplies every agent

right.title: Withdrawal danger ranking
points: Alcohol and benzodiazepines: seizures, delirium, death
Opioids: miserable, dangerous by dehydration and relapse
Stimulants: crash, depression, suicidality watch
Nicotine and caffeine: uncomfortable, safe

steps.tx: **Narcolepsy** prescribing inverts the stimulant lesson usefully: modafinil or solriamfetol and pitolisant for daytime sleepiness, sodium oxybate at night consolidating sleep and treating cataplexy (a controlled drug with respiratory cautions), stimulants as older alternatives, and anticataplectic antidepressants (venlafaxine) off label. The disorder's hypocretin deficiency is the same orexin system suvorexant blocks for insomnia in the sedative lessons, a symmetry examinations reward when both modules are read as one pharmacology.
steps.say: Narcolepsy is orexin missing; insomnia drugs block what narcolepsy lacks, and the examiners know you know.

nodes.label: Hypocretin deficiency destabilises sleep wake borders
Daytime: modafinil, solriamfetol, pitolisant or stimulants
Cataplexy covered by oxybate or antidepressant effect
